eligible_revision: Current master or explicitly designated current public-bounty release; exact commit required.

status_definitions.implementation_status: Existence of the offered public computation/checking boundary, not a hardness proof.
status_definitions.regression_status: Outcome of mapped regression cases at the stated baseline; not a security guarantee.
status_definitions.bounty_status: Technical target eligibility under this scope; no reward amount or payment terms implied.
status_definitions.security_proof: Proof status of the complete claimed property. Component primitives do not imply a reduction for the whole construction.

withheld_meaning: Not offered security properties of Public Bounty v1; absence is not a vulnerability in this scoped offering.
severity_rule: High 1-3 do not automatically become Critical 5. Classify the demonstrated acceptance/cryptanalytic failure.

targets.name: Canonical commitment collision
targets.description: Find distinct accepted high-entropy production inputs with an identical complete canonical commitment.
known_limitations: Regressions establish vector/encoding behavior, not collision resistance.
Input entropy is a generation property; type and length alone do not establish it.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Supply both distinct accepted inputs, high-entropy generation/search method, identical profile output and successful replay verification under the supported profile.

targets.name: Preimage or equivalent-preimage recovery
targets.description: Recover an accepted preimage of a high-entropy public challenge with substantially less work than generic brute force.
known_limitations: No formal PDE hardness reduction is claimed.
A passing regression is not evidence of a preimage complexity lower bound.
targets.valid_attack_definition: For an independently generated challenge with >=128 bits of input entropy, return accepted bytes such that verify_consensus_commitment(challenge, recovered) is True. Account for preprocessing, online work, memory and success probability against the same brute-force distribution.

targets.name: Supported consensus nondeterminism
targets.description: Find different profile outputs for the same valid input entirely within supported configurations.
known_limitations: CI tests specific platform/dependency combinations; it does not prove all compatible combinations deterministic.
The prior CPU-dispatch defect is fixed and retained as historical evidence.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Reproduce differing canonical bytes/commitments for one accepted input with exact environment details and no unsupported execution mode or modified reference implementation.
nonqualifying_examples: Changing the reference vector to permit disagreement

targets.name: Computation replay verification bypass
targets.description: Make the normative verifier accept an invalid input/state/invariant/profile declaration.
known_limitations: Computation replay requires the verifier to possess the candidate input.
It is not runtime attestation or authentication of arbitrary application context.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Supply an invalid declaration for input, state, invariants, kernel/parameters, profile/backend, canonical bytes or commitment and show actual successful replay acceptance. Context claims must also cross the public authentication verifier that binds them.
nonqualifying_examples: Exception or crash without invalid acceptance
Calling encoding consistency a proof of input provenance
Valid equivalent preimage without analyzing its cryptanalytic cause

targets.name: Canonical or semantic binding bypass
targets.description: Find a deeper authenticated-state binding failure after documented canonicalization rules hold.
known_limitations: High 1-3 do not automatically become Critical 5.
Regression coverage is not a proof excluding all semantic binding attacks.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Demonstrate semantic aliasing, an independently valid second canonical representation beyond High 1-3, producer/verifier state confusion, or authenticated body/metadata ambiguity surviving canonical verification.

targets.name: Noncanonical serialization acceptance
targets.description: Accept a prohibited noncanonical commitment preimage.
known_limitations: Canonical-byte validation establishes encoding consistency, not input provenance.
targets.valid_attack_definition: A normative byte/artifact verifier accepts an otherwise valid state with prohibited preimage encoding, schema, endian, dtype or layout representation.

targets.name: Nonfinite acceptance
targets.description: Accept NaN or either infinity in a prohibited security-relevant value.
known_limitations: Underflow to finite zero is allowed by the profile.
targets.valid_attack_definition: The normative production, serialization or verification path accepts NaN, +Inf or -Inf in a security-relevant state/invariant/profile field where the profile forbids it.
nonqualifying_examples: NaN in unrelated unconsumed application data

targets.name: Signed-zero divergence
targets.description: Produce divergent valid encodings/commitments for one logical state differing only by zero sign.
known_limitations: Zero-sign equivalence does not equate nonzero values or different inputs automatically.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Show valid canonical outputs for +0.0 and -0.0 representations of the same state that differ after normative normalization.
nonqualifying_examples: Changing an ordinary negative nonzero value
Raw negative-zero bytes rejected by byte validation

targets.name: Production input boundary bypass
targets.description: Admit an integer/string/demo mode or fewer than 16 bytes as normative production input.
known_limitations: The implementation checks exact bytes type and length; it does not measure statistical entropy.
targets.valid_attack_definition: The unmodified normative producer accepts an integer, string, demo seed mode or raw byte string shorter than 16 bytes.
nonqualifying_examples: Predictable but adequately sized bytes described as an entropy-check bypass

targets.name: Unsupported backend leakage
targets.description: An unsupported execution mode is incorrectly admitted as normative consensus output.
known_limitations: An artifact and its metadata do not remotely attest which machine executed a computation.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Demonstrate an actual supported API bypass in which unsupported backend/GPU/CuPy/fast-math/reassociation or alternate profile output is emitted and accepted as WL-Consensus-Commitment-v1.
nonqualifying_examples: Replacing/monkeypatching trusted producer or verifier code
Independently producing equivalent valid bytes outside the supported API without demonstrating incorrect API admission; artifacts are not runtime attestations.

targets.name: One-time identity and reuse acceptance
targets.description: Accept a consumed one-time key or leaf as fresh through stateful verification.
known_limitations: Lamport-style OTS remains vulnerable to intentional key reuse; the offered boundary is default signing/stateful acceptance.
No global distributed replay consensus is claimed.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Show two successful stateful acceptances of one consumed key/leaf in the shared public acceptance state, or bypass the default local signer-use guard while retaining its state.
nonqualifying_examples: Repeated pure verify_ots calls returning True
Independent isolated ledgers presented as one shared ledger

targets.name: Body transcript and authenticated context binding
targets.description: Accept unauthorized body/transcript/metadata under an existing signature.
known_limitations: Transcript v1 is preserved; its exact public metadata boundary determines what is authenticated.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Mutate signed body, transcript, authenticated metadata, block type or parent and show authentication/normal acceptance under the existing authorization.
nonqualifying_examples: A newly authorized block with a fresh key
Arbitrary unsigned application fields outside the offered record
A verifier rejecting the modified transcript

targets.name: Public-key fingerprint and Merkle consistency
targets.description: Pass public OTS verification with inconsistent identity or committed key material.
known_limitations: The public construction validates its complete committed-key/Merkle-root structure; no broader tree signing service is implied.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Supply a substituted public key, mismatched fingerprint/Merkle root/commitment array or modified revealed slice and obtain successful public authentication.
nonqualifying_examples: Generating a different valid key and signing a new authorization
Claiming an unimplemented arbitrary Merkle-path protocol

targets.name: Authenticated header and chain linkage integrity
targets.description: Accept unauthorized stable header changes or mutated authenticated records into valid chain linkage.
known_limitations: Unanchored history completeness and trustworthy checkpoint acquisition are withheld, not offered properties.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Modify authenticated version/index/timestamp/difficulty/context or a linked authenticated record and show normal v2 chain acceptance despite the unauthorized mutation.
nonqualifying_examples: A valid chain prefix without a trusted external tip

targets.name: Persistent replay parsing and restart reconstruction
targets.description: Bypass public replay-record schema checks or offered restart reconstruction.
known_limitations: Unsigned replay-cache authenticity against arbitrary hostile writes is withheld.
Separate replay/chain files may burn a key before block append; Windows has no portable directory-fsync power-loss guarantee.
targets.valid_attack_definition: A malformed schema/version/identifier record is treated as valid, or restart/cache-loss reconstruction with accepted history retained permits consumed-identity acceptance. Unauthorized reuse demonstrates Critical AR-1 impact.
nonqualifying_examples: Rollback/deletion of all authoritative local state
A conservatively burned key that cannot be reused

targets.name: Same-host process-race exclusion
targets.description: Race shared public state into duplicate acceptance or incompatible sibling appends.
known_limitations: Local file/SQLite exclusion is not distributed consensus.
Filesystem must provide the documented atomic publication and lock semantics.
targets.valid_attack_definition: Synchronize competing processes sharing the same normal data/replay paths and demonstrate successful duplicate one-time acceptance or inconsistent sibling appends.
nonqualifying_examples: Two separate hosts or isolated data directories
Bypassing the public acceptance path with direct historical file writes

withheld_targets.name: Remote runtime/machine/kernel/configuration attestation
withheld_targets.reason: Requires a separate trust architecture not provided by the public reference repository.

withheld_targets.name: Behavior-wide drift-detection evasion
withheld_targets.reason: The public repository does not provide the observation/enforcement boundary needed for this broader claim.

withheld_targets.name: Broad hostile rollback/cache tamper/trusted-anchor guarantees
withheld_targets.reason: Public authenticated records and local persistence checks do not provide a complete hostile-host rollback-resistant system. Only AR-1 through AR-6 are offered.
